accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the habitat of an organism?
o: The physical place where the organism lives
The total number of organisms in a population
The functional role performed by the organism in an ecosystem
The climatic region containing similar vegetation
accepted.x: Habitat is the physical place where an organism lives. Its functional role is described by the term niche.
accepted.tq: Use the habitat–niche distinction and identify the physical-location meaning.
accepted.sec: Ecology terms - habitat, niche, population attributes, community, biome, ecotone, resistance, resilience

accepted.s: The term ‘niche’ refers to which one of the following?
o: The total population of different species in an area
The transition zone between two ecosystems
The functional role of an organism, including the food, space, time and conditions it uses
The physical area occupied by an organism
accepted.x: A niche is the functional role of an organism and includes the food, space, time and environmental conditions it uses.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the physical place, habitat, and the functional role, niche.
accepted.sec: Ecology terms - habitat, niche, population attributes, community, biome, ecotone, resistance, resilience

accepted.s: Natality in a population is concerned with
o: the number of individuals dying in a population
the number of births in a population
the proportion of males and females in a population
the distribution of individuals among age groups
accepted.x: Natality means births in a population. Its rate may be expressed as the number of individuals produced per female per unit time.
accepted.tq: Match the population attribute with the process it measures.
accepted.sec: Ecology terms - habitat, niche, population attributes, community, biome, ecotone, resistance, resilience

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a population attribute?
accepted.x: Density, mortality, age structure and sex ratio are population attributes. Dominant vegetation is associated with the description of a biome.
accepted.tq: Find the item belonging to the neighbouring ecological level rather than the population level.
accepted.sec: Ecology terms - habitat, niche, population attributes, community, biome, ecotone, resistance, resilience

accepted.s: A community in ecology consists of
o: all abiotic factors in a habitat
all individuals of one species in an area
all populations of different species in an area
accepted.x: A community comprises all populations of different species living in an area.
accepted.tq: Separate a community from a single-species population by checking the word ‘different’.
accepted.sec: Ecology terms - habitat, niche, population attributes, community, biome, ecotone, resistance, resilience

accepted.s: A biome is primarily defined by its
o: number of species at an ecosystem boundary
accepted.x: A biome is a large region defined by climate and dominant vegetation, such as rainforest, tundra or desert.
accepted.tq: Identify the defining pair in a classification question: climate plus dominant vegetation.
accepted.sec: Ecology terms - habitat, niche, population attributes, community, biome, ecotone, resistance, resilience

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. An ecotone is a transition zone between two ecosystems.
2. Ecotones may show greater species richness because of the edge effect.
3. Mangroves and estuaries can exemplify ecotones.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. An ecotone is a transition zone, and its boundary conditions may produce an edge effect and increased species richness.
accepted.tq: Check whether all statements describe the definition, examples and characteristic effect of an ecotone.
accepted.sec: Ecology terms - habitat, niche, population attributes, community, biome, ecotone, resistance, resilience

accepted.s: The ability of an ecosystem to withstand a disturbance is known as
accepted.x: Resistance is the ability to withstand disturbance. Resilience is the ability to recover after disturbance.
accepted.tq: Separate the two similar terms by asking whether the ecosystem withstands or recovers from disturbance.
accepted.sec: Ecology terms - habitat, niche, population attributes, community, biome, ecotone, resistance, resilience

accepted.s: The ability of an ecosystem to recover after a disturbance is called
accepted.x: Resilience refers to the ability to recover after a disturbance, whereas resistance refers to withstanding it.
accepted.tq: Test the recovery meaning of resilience against the withstand meaning of resistance.
accepted.sec: Ecology terms - habitat, niche, population attributes, community, biome, ecotone, resistance, resilience

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations is most consistent with greater ecological stability?
o: Lower diversity and a simpler food web
A single producer and a single consumer
Higher diversity and greater food-web complexity
accepted.x: Ecological stability generally rises with increasing diversity and greater food-web complexity.
accepted.tq: Apply the relationship between diversity, web complexity and ecosystem stability.
accepted.sec: Ecology terms - habitat, niche, population attributes, community, biome, ecotone, resistance, resilience

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding ecological pyramids is correct?
o: The base represents top consumers and the apex represents producers.
The base generally represents producers and the apex represents top consumers.
Ecological pyramids have only two types.
All organisms occupy only one trophic level.
accepted.x: The base of an ecological pyramid represents producers and the apex represents top consumers. The three types are pyramids of number, biomass and energy.
accepted.tq: Use the structural rule of ecological pyramids: producers at the base and top consumers at the apex.
accepted.sec: Ecological pyramids - number, biomass, energy; upright and inverted cases

accepted.s: How many major types of ecological pyramids are recognised in the classification given below?
accepted.x: The three major types are the pyramid of number, the pyramid of biomass and the pyramid of energy.
accepted.tq: Count the named categories rather than confusing ecological pyramids with trophic levels.
accepted.sec: Ecological pyramids - number, biomass, energy; upright and inverted cases

accepted.s: A pyramid of numbers is likely to be inverted in
o: a tree ecosystem with one tree supporting many insects
a simple grazing chain beginning with grasses
a crop field with many plants
accepted.x: A tree ecosystem may have one producer tree supporting numerous herbivorous insects, producing an inverted pyramid of numbers.
accepted.tq: Visualise the number of organisms at each level instead of their size or biomass.
accepted.sec: Ecological pyramids - number, biomass, energy; upright and inverted cases

accepted.s: An inverted pyramid of numbers may also occur in
o: a forest floor litter chain only
accepted.x: Parasitic food chains can have fewer hosts supporting numerous parasites, resulting in an inverted pyramid of numbers.
accepted.tq: Recognise the host–parasite pattern as a standard exception to an upright number pyramid.
accepted.sec: Ecological pyramids - number, biomass, energy; upright and inverted cases

accepted.s: In which one of the following ecosystems is an inverted pyramid of biomass characteristically observed?
accepted.x: In aquatic ecosystems, the small standing biomass of rapidly multiplying phytoplankton can support a larger biomass of zooplankton and fish.
accepted.tq: Compare standing biomass in terrestrial systems with rapidly turning-over phytoplankton in aquatic systems.
accepted.sec: Ecological pyramids - number, biomass, energy; upright and inverted cases

accepted.s: Why can the biomass pyramid in an aquatic ecosystem be inverted?
o: Fish do not consume zooplankton in aquatic ecosystems.
Energy increases at every aquatic trophic level.
Phytoplankton have a small standing crop but rapidly support larger zooplankton and fish biomass.
accepted.x: Phytoplankton have a small standing crop but reproduce and are consumed rapidly, allowing them to support a larger standing biomass of zooplankton and fish.
accepted.tq: Distinguish standing biomass from productivity and identify the fast-turnover producer explanation.
accepted.sec: Ecological pyramids - number, biomass, energy; upright and inverted cases

accepted.s: Which ecological pyramid can NEVER be inverted?
accepted.x: The energy pyramid is always upright because energy is lost as heat at every trophic transfer and cannot increase at higher levels.
accepted.tq: Look for the absolute exception and connect it with energy loss at each trophic transfer.
accepted.sec: Ecological pyramids - number, biomass, energy; upright and inverted cases

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Energy is lost as heat at every trophic transfer.
2. Therefore, the energy pyramid is always upright.
3. A single species may occupy more than one trophic level in a food web.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Heat loss keeps the energy pyramid upright, while omnivory may allow one species to occupy more than one trophic level.
accepted.tq: Link the physical rule of energy loss with the food-web exception concerning trophic levels.
accepted.sec: Ecological pyramids - number, biomass, energy; upright and inverted cases

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Pyramid)
a. Number
b. Biomass
c. Energy
List-II (Characteristic)
i. Always upright
 ii. May be inverted in aquatic ecosystems
 iii. May be inverted in a tree ecosystem

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: The pyramid of number may be inverted in a tree ecosystem, the biomass pyramid may be inverted in aquatic systems, and the energy pyramid is always upright.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair that energy is always upright, then match the two inversion cases.
accepted.sec: Ecological pyramids - number, biomass, energy; upright and inverted cases

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents producers in a terrestrial ecosystem?
o: Sulphur bacteria at deep-sea vents only
accepted.x: Herbs, shrubs and trees are the principal producers in terrestrial ecosystems.
accepted.tq: Match the producer group with its ecosystem rather than with an aquatic or vent environment.
accepted.sec: Producers in different ecosystems - terrestrial, aquatic, chemosynthetic

accepted.s: In an aquatic ecosystem, the producer group includes
o: phytoplankton, algae, and submerged and floating plants
accepted.x: Aquatic producers include phytoplankton, algae, and submerged and floating plants.
accepted.tq: Identify organisms capable of primary production in water and exclude aquatic consumers.
accepted.sec: Producers in different ecosystems - terrestrial, aquatic, chemosynthetic

accepted.s: The primary producers at deep-sea vents are chiefly
accepted.x: Chemosynthetic bacteria, including sulphur bacteria, use chemical energy rather than light at deep-sea vents.
accepted.tq: Apply the light-versus-chemical-energy distinction to a lightless ecosystem.
accepted.sec: Producers in different ecosystems - terrestrial, aquatic, chemosynthetic

accepted.s: A species whose effect on a community is far greater than would be expected from its abundance is called a
accepted.x: A keystone species has an ecological effect far larger than its abundance; its removal may cause the community to collapse.
accepted.tq: Use the defining phrase ‘effect far larger than abundance’ to identify a keystone species.
accepted.sec: Species roles - keystone, foundation, flagship, indicator, umbrella

accepted.s: The sea star Pisaster ochraceus is regarded as a keystone species because it
accepted.x: Pisaster ochraceus is a keystone sea star that controls mussels in intertidal zones. This example is associated with the work of Robert Paine.
accepted.tq: Use the species–ecological effect association rather than the general definition alone.
accepted.sec: Species roles - keystone, foundation, flagship, indicator, umbrella

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a foundation species?
accepted.x: Foundation species create or shape the habitat itself; corals and kelp are examples.
accepted.tq: Distinguish habitat-building species from charismatic and environmental-indicator species.
accepted.sec: Species roles - keystone, foundation, flagship, indicator, umbrella

accepted.s: A species selected to draw public support for conservation because of its charismatic appeal is known as a
accepted.x: A flagship species is a charismatic species used to draw public support for conservation; the tiger and giant panda are examples.
accepted.tq: Identify the public-support function rather than an ecosystem-function role.
accepted.sec: Species roles - keystone, foundation, flagship, indicator, umbrella

accepted.s: Lichens are commonly used as indicators of
accepted.x: Lichens can indicate environmental health and are particularly used as indicators of sulphur dioxide pollution.
accepted.tq: Match the indicator organism with the environmental condition it signals.
accepted.sec: Species roles - keystone, foundation, flagship, indicator, umbrella

accepted.s: The umbrella species concept implies that protection of a wide-ranging species
o: always increases the number of producers
protects many other species sharing its habitat
accepted.x: Protecting a wide-ranging umbrella species can protect many other species that share its habitat and range.
accepted.tq: Apply the spatial-cover meaning of an umbrella species to a conservation situation.
accepted.sec: Species roles - keystone, foundation, flagship, indicator, umbrella

accepted.s: Which pair is NOT correctly matched?
o: Keystone species — effect much larger than its abundance
Umbrella species — attracts public support mainly through charisma
Foundation species — creates or shapes habitat
accepted.x: Attracting public support through charisma is the role of a flagship species. An umbrella species is wide-ranging, and its protection benefits many other species.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped definition among closely related conservation roles.
accepted.sec: Species roles - keystone, foundation, flagship, indicator, umbrella

accepted.s: Which adaptation is characteristic of halophytes growing in saline soils or mangroves?
o: Reduced roots and floating leaves only
Absence of any specialised root system
accepted.x: Halophytes may possess pneumatophores for breathing, salt glands and vivipary; mangrove plants such as Rhizophora are examples.
accepted.tq: Match the habitat type with its distinctive structural adaptations.
accepted.sec: Habitat adaptations - halophytes, xerophytes, hydrophytes

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly associated with xerophytes?
o: Thin cuticle and reduced roots for floating
Thick cuticle, sunken stomata, spines, succulence and CAM
accepted.x: Xerophytes are adapted to deserts through features such as thick cuticles, sunken stomata, spines, succulence and CAM; Opuntia is an example.
accepted.tq: Recognise the water-conservation package typical of desert plants.
accepted.sec: Habitat adaptations - halophytes, xerophytes, hydrophytes

accepted.s: Aerenchyma, reduced roots, thin cuticle and floating leaves are characteristic adaptations of
accepted.x: Hydrophytes are water plants and commonly possess aerenchyma, reduced roots, thin cuticles and floating leaves. Hydrilla and lotus are examples.
accepted.tq: Match the structural features with the water-adapted plant group.
accepted.sec: Habitat adaptations - halophytes, xerophytes, hydrophytes

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Rhizophora — halophyte
2. Opuntia — xerophyte
3. Hydrilla — hydrophyte
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correct. Rhizophora is a salt-tolerant mangrove plant, Opuntia is a desert plant, and Hydrilla is an aquatic plant.
accepted.tq: Verify each organism against its habitat adaptation before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Habitat adaptations - halophytes, xerophytes, hydrophytes
